opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees max out at write, and admin would require the role to own Payroll (Payroll Specialist), which does not apply. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E045 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, and admin is never allowed. The requested write level for Payroll is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR indicates full-time (which would allow write), while Security DB indicates contractor with basic security training (which caps at read, since write requires advanced training for contractors). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive interpretation consistent with least privilege: E045 is a contractor with basic training, so the maximum allowed level for Payroll is read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant read.
